title: The Simulation Modeling Software Database — Overview: software that runs the world twice
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Simulation modeling software runs the world twice — once in the computer, once in reality — so the first run can be wrong safely. Block-diagram tools model dynamic systems as wired blocks; discrete-event tools model queues and processes as event lists; agent-based tools model crowds and markets as interacting individuals; finite-element tools model structures as meshes; CFD tools model fluids as grids. Each record below covers a real tool with a working demo in its spirit.
capabilities: Five simulation paradigms with honest comparisons
Seven real tools, each with a working demo
Why simulate: safe wrongness before real wrongness
Validation: the simulation must meet measurement

title: The Simulation Modeling Software Database — Simulink
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Simulink, from MathWorks, is the block-diagram environment for modeling dynamic systems: drag integrator, gain, and sum blocks onto a canvas, wire them, and press run. Control engineers design autopilots and motor controllers in it, generating C code for embedded targets from the same diagram. It pairs with MATLAB and is commercial software. The demo integrates a decaying system the way a Simulink integrator block does — Euler steps, visible and honest.
capabilities: MathWorks block-diagram dynamic simulation
Integrator, gain, and sum blocks wired on canvas
C code generation for embedded targets
Control systems: autopilots and motor controllers

title: The Simulation Modeling Software Database — AnyLogic
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. AnyLogic, from The AnyLogic Company, is the multimethod simulator: agent-based, discrete-event, and system-dynamics models can live in one project. Supply chains, pedestrian crowds, and epidemics are its classic subjects — wherever individual behavior creates system behavior. It is Java-based and commercial, with a free personal learning edition. The demo runs a tiny agent model: walkers on a line, counting how many reach the target zone.
capabilities: Multimethod: agents, discrete events, system dynamics together
Supply chains, crowds, and epidemics as classic subjects
Java-based, commercial with free learning edition
Emergence: system behavior from individual rules

title: The Simulation Modeling Software Database — Arena
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Arena, from Rockwell Automation, is discrete-event simulation for processes: model the factory, the call center, or the emergency room as entities flowing through stations, seizing resources, and waiting in queues. Its flowchart-style modules make the logic visible to non-programmers, and its analyzers report throughput, utilization, and waiting times. Commercial software with deep roots in manufacturing. The demo runs a miniature event queue: arrivals, one server, measured waits.
capabilities: Rockwell Automation discrete-event simulation
Entities, stations, resources, and queues
Flowchart modules visible to non-programmers
Throughput, utilization, and waiting-time reports

title: The Simulation Modeling Software Database — ANSYS
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. ANSYS is the finite-element giant: structures, fluids, electromagnetics, and heat transfer solved on meshes of the real geometry. Engineers crash cars, cool chips, and quiet cabins in it before building anything. Its Mechanical and Fluent products are industry standards, commercial and premium-priced. The demo solves a two-element bar in the finite-element spirit: assemble stiffness, apply load, read displacement.
capabilities: Finite-element multiphysics: structures, fluids, EM, heat
Mechanical and Fluent as industry standards
Meshing real geometry, solving real physics
Commercial, premium, everywhere in engineering

title: The Simulation Modeling Software Database — OpenFOAM
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. OpenFOAM is the open-source CFD toolbox: finite-volume solvers for incompressible and compressible flow, turbulence, heat transfer, and multiphase problems, free for anyone to download and extend. Researchers and startups run real aerodynamics and process engineering in it without license fees. The demo advects a pulse down a line with the upwind scheme — the honest workhorse of CFD discretization.
capabilities: Open-source finite-volume CFD toolbox
Incompressible, compressible, turbulence, multiphase solvers
Free to download, extend, and commercialize
The researcher and startup choice

title: The Simulation Modeling Software Database — Modelica
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Modelica is an equation-based, object-oriented language for modeling physical systems — write the equations, and the tool sorts out causality. Libraries like the Modelica Standard Library cover mechanics, electrics, hydraulics, and heat transfer with reusable components. OpenModelica provides a free environment; commercial tools like Dymola compile models fast. The demo integrates an RC circuit the equation-based way: state the differential equation, step it.
capabilities: Equation-based, object-oriented modeling language
Write equations; the tool sorts causality
Standard library: mechanics, electrics, hydraulics, heat
OpenModelica free; Dymola commercial

title: The Simulation Modeling Software Database — NetLogo
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. NetLogo, from Northwestern University, is the agent-based modeling environment that taught a generation: turtles move on patches, following simple rules, and complex patterns emerge. Free and education-focused, its models library covers segregation, flocking, fire spread, and market dynamics. The demo diffuses heat across a patch grid for one step — emergence from local rules, the NetLogo way.
capabilities: Northwestern: agent-based modeling for education
Turtles on patches, simple rules, emergent patterns
Free with a vast models library
Segregation, flocking, fire spread classics
